      - "R²: DINO (0.634) ≈ Proj (0.630) > CLIP (0.587). last_preaction R²=0.671 (readout concentration, p=0.002 vs Proj)."
      - "LLM inverted-U: L0=0.612 → L12=0.628 (peak, above projector 0.615) → L32=0.422."
      - "Training peak shift: best-vs-best Δ=+0.017 n.s.; same-layer L12 Δ=+0.079 p<0.0001."

  - name: Introduction
    structure:
      - para_1_problem: >
          VLAs achieve impressive manipulation performance by fine-tuning LLMs on robot data.
          Implicit assumption: fine-tuning injects action-relevant representational knowledge.
          But where do action representations actually come from?
      - para_2_gap: >
          Grant et al. 2026 showed visual pathway dominates at behavioral level.
          Hou 2026 / Fei 2025 showed VLAs largely ignore language instructions.
          But no work has performed representational decomposition — measuring each component's
          independent contribution to action-relevant structure, nor traced action geometry
          through the LLM's 33 layers.
      - para_3_approach: >
          We systematically decompose OpenVLA: extract representations from
          (1) standalone vision encoders (DINOv2, CLIP), (2) fused backbone + projector,
          (3) LLM at every layer (image_mean + last_preaction), comparing trained vs untrained
          LLM × instruction conditions. RSA (geometric alignment), CKA (global structure),
          and functional probes (action prediction R²).
      - para_4_findings: >
          Three findings: (1) Self-supervised DINOv2 provides strongest action-aligned geometry
          (cls RSA=0.692), outperforming VL-pretrained CLIP (0.557). VL pretraining does not
          enhance action-relevant structure. (2) LLM transformation is non-monotonic:
          first 12 layers enhance geometric alignment (0.612→0.628, surpassing projector 0.615),
          final 20 layers degrade it (→0.422). CKA monotonically rises, revealing metric-level
          dissociation. (3) Training redistributes action signal (peak shift L0→L12) without
          creating new knowledge (best-vs-best Δ=+0.017, n.s.). Instruction content has no
          effect (|Δ|<0.006).
      - para_5_implications: >
          Implications for VLA design: vision encoder pretraining quality (especially
          self-supervised) is the primary lever; LLM's early layers enhance geometry while
          late layers degrade it; training teaches redistribution not creation.
    core_evidence:
      - d041_method_b_rsa
      - plan_012_clip_vit_control
      - plan_013_branch_split
      - unified_action_probe
      - d041_training_effect_bootstrap

  - name: Related Work

    positioning: >
      Grant et al. 2026 is closest — we confirm their behavioral finding at representation level
      with quantitative component decomposition + per-layer curves. Key difference: they find
      "visual pathway dominates," we further show self-supervised (DINO) > VL-pretrained (CLIP)

      controls (trained/untrained × instruction ablation). Haon et al. same venue+model —
      complementary (sparse semantic directions vs geometric analysis).

  - name: Method
    subsections:
      - name: "2.1 Model and Data"
        content_outline: >
          OpenVLA architecture: DinoSigLIP fused backbone (DINOv2 ViT-L 1024d + SigLIP-SO400M
          1152d → torch.cat → 2176d) → MLP projector (2176→4096) → Llama-2 7B (33 layers)
          → action head. Base OpenVLA-7B checkpoint (OXE-pretrained on 970K episodes),
          NOT fine-tuned on LIBERO. "Trained" = OXE-pretrained LLM weights;
          "Untrained" = LLM weights randomly reinitialized (vision encoder + projector
          identical, cos_sim=1.0). LIBERO-Goal benchmark: 10 tasks, 50 demos/task.
      - name: "2.2 Representation Extraction"
        content_outline: >
          Ten representation sources spanning three levels:
          (a) Standalone encoders: DINOv2 cls_token, DINOv2 patch_mean, CLIP ViT-L/14 cls_token;
          (b) Fused backbone: DinoSigLIP 2176d (+ branch-split: DINOv2 1024d, SigLIP 1152d);
          (c) After projector: SigLIP+Projector 4096d;
          (d) LLM per-layer: image_mean (mean of image tokens at each of 33 layers),
              last_preaction (readout token = last token before action prediction);
          2×2 conditions for LLM: trained/untrained × with-instruction/no-instruction.
      - name: "2.3 Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA)"
        content_outline: >
          Method B: within-task pairing + euclidean action distance + full trajectory,
          50 demos/task. Construct RDMs for representations and 7-D action space.
          Spearman correlation between upper-triangular RDM vectors.
          Per-task RSA aggregated across tasks.
          Bootstrap CI (10,000 resamples) for pairwise comparisons.
      - name: "2.4 Functional Action Probes"
        content_outline: >
          Unified hyperparams: MLP probe (Linear→ReLU→Linear, input_dim→256→7;
          Adam lr=1e-3, batch=256, epochs=50, early stopping patience=5, seed=42)
          trained on representation→action mapping. Mean R² across 7 action dimensions.
          Per-task train/val splits. Bootstrap paired comparison for statistical significance.
          Also: action-delta probes (predict Δaction = a_{t+1} - a_t).
          All R² from unified_action_probe with standardized hyperparameters.
      - name: "2.5 CKA Analysis"
        content_outline: >
          Linear CKA and RDM-based CKA as complementary metric to RSA.
          Motivation: RSA captures local geometric alignment, CKA captures global structure.
          Per-layer CKA curves to compare with RSA inverted-U trajectory.

  - name: Experiments
    subsections:
      - name: "3.1 Experimental Setup"
        content_outline: >
          LIBERO-Goal benchmark: 10 manipulation tasks, 50 demos each.
          Method B RSA protocol (within-task + euclidean + full trajectory).
          Representation extraction pipeline. Statistical testing protocol
          (bootstrap 10K, permutation). Hardware: 2× GPU on westd-19183.

      - name: "3.2 Vision Encoder Dominance (Claim 1)"
        core_evidence:
          - d041_method_b_rsa            # DINO cls=0.692, patch_mean=0.631
          - plan_012_clip_vit_control    # CLIP RSA=0.557, R²=0.587
          - plan_013_branch_split        # DINOv2 branch=0.619, SigLIP branch=0.621, Fused=0.634
          - unified_action_probe         # R²: DINO 0.634 ≈ Proj 0.630 > CLIP 0.587
        key_numbers:
          - "DINO cls_token RSA=0.692 — highest across all feature sources"
          - "Cross-encoder ranking: DINO patch_mean (0.631) > SigLIP+Proj (0.615) > CLIP (0.557)"
          - "Branch-split: DINOv2 1024d (0.619) ≈ SigLIP 1152d (0.621); Fused 2176d (0.634) > either branch"
          - "Projector compression: Fused 0.634 → Proj 0.615 (MLP 2176→4096)"
          - "R² ranking: DINO (0.634) ≈ Proj (0.630) > CLIP (0.587); RSA and R² orderings agree"
          - "Self-supervised DINOv2 > VL-pretrained CLIP in both geometry and function → VL pretraining does not enhance action structure"
        structure: >
          (a) Cross-encoder RSA: DINO cls (0.692) > DINO patch_mean (0.631) > SigLIP+Proj (0.615)
              > CLIP (0.557). Self-supervised DINO dominates, VL pretraining does not help.
          (b) Branch-split: DinoSigLIP fused (0.634) has roughly equal contributions from
              DINOv2 branch (0.619) and SigLIP branch (0.621). Projector MLP compresses 0.634→0.615.
          (c) Functional probe: R² ordering consistent — DINO (0.634) ≈ Proj (0.630) > CLIP (0.587).
              RSA and R² rankings agree; no geometric-functional dissociation.
          (d) CLIP as VL-pretraining control: CLIP (0.557) < DINO (0.631/0.692),
              confirming VL pretraining is NOT the source of action-relevant structure.

      - name: "3.3 LLM Non-Monotonic Transformation (Claim 2)"
        core_evidence:
          - d041_method_b_rsa            # Per-layer inverted-U curve
          - plan_009_cka_verification    # CKA monotonic rise, metric dissociation
          - unified_action_probe         # last_preaction R²=0.671 > Proj 0.630
        key_numbers:
          - "Trained image_mean inverted-U: L0=0.612 → L12=0.628 (peak) → L32=0.422"
          - "L12 peak (0.628) > projector input (0.615) — first 12 layers enhance geometry"
          - "Untrained image_mean monotonic decay: L0=0.612 → L12=0.550 → L32=0.545"
          - "CKA monotonic rise: L0=0.081 → L32=0.098 (global structure preserved)"
          - "RSA inverted-U vs CKA monotonic rise → metric-level dissociation"
          - "Readout concentration: trained last_preaction peak L12 RSA=0.643"
          - "Functional: last_preaction R²=0.671 > projector 0.630 (p=0.002)"
          - "image_mean R²=0.599 < projector 0.630 (p<0.001)"
        structure: >
          (a) Per-layer RSA curve: trained image_mean shows inverted-U — first 12 layers enhance
              geometric alignment beyond projector input (0.612→0.628>0.615), last 20 layers
              degrade (→0.422). Untrained shows monotonic decay from L0.
          (b) Enhancement is training-dependent: only trained model shows inverted-U; untrained
              model decays monotonically from L0=0.612.
          (c) Readout concentration: trained last_preaction RSA=0.643 at L12, surpassing
              all image_mean values. Functional probe confirms: last_preaction R²=0.671 > Proj 0.630 (p=0.002).
          (d) CKA complement: CKA monotonically rises L0→L32, while RSA has inverted-U.
              LLM changes local geometric alignment while preserving global structure.
              Metric-level dissociation — interpretation depends on metric choice.

      - name: "3.4 Training Redistributes, Doesn't Create (Claim 3)"
        core_evidence:
          - d041_training_effect_bootstrap  # Best-vs-best and same-layer comparisons
          - d041_method_b_rsa               # Peak shift L0→L12
          - plan_008_random_inst_control    # Instruction invariance
          - plan_004_output_head_analysis   # Vision backbone identical
        key_numbers:
          - "Peak shift: untrained peaks at L0, trained peaks at L12"
          - "Best-vs-best (trained L12 vs untrained L0): Δ=+0.017, CI includes 0, n.s."
          - "Same-layer L12: trained 0.628 vs untrained 0.550, Δ=+0.079, p<0.0001"
          - "Instruction invariance image_mean: max |Δ|=0.006 (normal/random/shuffled/empty)"
          - "Instruction invariance last_preaction: max |Δ|=0.017"
          - "Vision backbone + projector: identical weights (cos_sim=1.0) between trained/untrained"
        structure: >
          (a) Peak shift: training moves RSA peak from L0 (untrained) to L12 (trained).
              This is redistribution of action signal across layers, not invariance.
          (b) Best-vs-best comparison: peak amplitudes are comparable (Δ=+0.017, n.s.) —
              training doesn't create new action-relevant structure, it redistributes.
          (c) Same-layer L12: Δ=+0.079, p<0.0001 — training concentrates signal
              at L12, which untrained model distributes differently.
          (d) Instruction invariance: max |Δ|=0.006 for image_mean, 0.017 for last_preaction.
              Instruction content does not modulate representation structure.
          (e) Functional confirmation: last_preaction R²=0.671 > Proj 0.630 (p=0.002) —
              training teaches readout concentration.

      - name: "3.5 Metric Sensitivity: RSA vs CKA (Supplementary or Main)"
        core_evidence:
          - plan_009_cka_verification
        key_numbers:
          - "Linear CKA: untrained(0.089) > trained(0.083) > proj(0.081) > DINO(0.066)"
          - "CKA per-layer trained image_mean: L0=0.081 → L32=0.098 — monotonic rise"
          - "CKA last_preaction: L32=0.127 (highest)"
          - "RSA inverted-U (peak L12) vs CKA monotonic rise — metric dissociation"
        structure: >
          RSA captures local geometric alignment, CKA captures global structure.
          RSA inverted-U vs CKA monotonic rise reveals LLM changes geometry while preserving
          global structure. CKA encoder ordering reverses RSA ordering.
          CKA last_preaction highest (0.127) — consistent with readout concentration.
          Could be main text subsection or supplementary depending on space.

  - name: Discussion
    structure:
      - para_1_synthesis: >
          Three findings form coherent picture: self-supervised vision encoder provides
          strongest action-aligned geometry (DINO cls 0.692), LLM non-monotonically transforms
          it (enhance first 12 layers, degrade last 20), training redistributes signal
          (peak shift L0→L12) without creating new knowledge.
      - para_2_self_supervised_dominance: >
          DINO (0.692/0.631) > CLIP (0.557) overturns the assumption that VL pretraining
          helps action representations. Self-supervised geometric learning (DINOv2's
          patch-level objectives) produces better action-aligned structure than
          vision-language contrastive learning. R² confirms: DINO (0.634) ≈ Proj (0.630) > CLIP (0.587).
      - para_3_branch_split_insight: >
          Branch-split reveals both branches contribute roughly equally (DINOv2 0.619, SigLIP 0.621)
          to the fused backbone (0.634). Projector MLP compresses rather than enhances (0.634→0.615).
          The standalone DINO cls_token (0.692) exceeding the fused backbone (0.634) suggests
          SigLIP concatenation may dilute DINOv2's geometric structure.
      - para_4_llm_transformation: >
          The inverted-U trajectory (enhance→degrade) is more nuanced than simple degradation.
          First 12 layers actively enhance geometric alignment beyond projector input
          (0.612→0.628>0.615), paralleling NLP findings that middle layers are most task-informative.
          CKA monotonic rise alongside RSA inverted-U shows LLM transforms local geometry
          while preserving global structure — metric choice determines narrative.
      - para_5_implications: >
          (1) Vision encoder pretraining quality is primary lever — self-supervised > VL-pretrained.
          (2) LLM early layers beneficial; consider early-exit for action extraction.
          (3) Training teaches redistribution (peak shift) not knowledge creation.
          (4) Language instructions do not modulate representation structure (|Δ|<0.006).
      - para_6_connection_to_behavioral: >
          Our representational findings explain Grant et al. 2026's behavioral results:
          vision dominates because the frozen encoder provides the action-relevant structure.
          We go further: within vision, self-supervised (DINO) > VL-pretrained (CLIP).
          "Encoded but not used" (their instruction finding) aligns with our instruction invariance.
      - para_7_limitations: >
          Single architecture (OpenVLA). Single benchmark suite (LIBERO-Goal).
          RSA captures structural alignment, not causal contribution.
          R² peak at L19 vs RSA peak at L12 — functional capacity may accumulate
          after geometric alignment begins declining (plan_011 pending).
          "Trained" = OXE-pretrained, not task-specific fine-tuned.
    core_evidence:
      - d041_method_b_rsa
      - plan_012_clip_vit_control
      - plan_013_branch_split
      - unified_action_probe
      - plan_009_cka_verification

  - name: Conclusion
    structure:
      - para_1_summary: >
          First systematic representational decomposition of a VLA. Three findings:
          (1) self-supervised vision encoder (DINOv2) provides strongest action-aligned geometry,
          outperforming VL-pretrained encoders — VL pretraining does not enhance action structure;
          (2) LLM non-monotonically transforms action geometry — first 12 layers enhance,
          last 20 layers degrade, while global structure (CKA) is preserved;
          (3) training redistributes action signal across layers (peak shift L0→L12)
          without creating new knowledge.
      - para_2_takeaway: >
          Action representations in VLAs are inherited from the vision encoder, not learned
          by the LLM. Design implications: invest in self-supervised vision encoder pretraining;
          LLM's early-layer enhancement suggests architectural opportunities;
          instruction content's null effect on representations demands rethinking language's role in VLAs.
